subject: Embeddings endpoint latency spike after model-catalog update — urgent customer escalation
messages:
From: Alex Garner <alex.garner@cartograph.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-team@cartograph.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden latency spikes on embeddings endpoint (p95/p99)

Vanessa,

We're seeing a sharp jump in embeddings latency this morning across multiple jobs: p95 has moved from ~160ms to ~1.8s and p99 to ~3.4s. Throughput is also degraded — batch jobs are timing out. This started right after we picked up the latest model-catalog tag (we followed the usual stable alias).

Can you confirm if anything changed on your side? Our SLAs are getting breached and product search is degraded. I've attached a short latency CSV and representative trace IDs.

-- Alex
Alex Garner
Head of Platform, Cartograph.ai
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Garner <alex.garner@cartograph.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: sudden latency spikes on embeddings endpoint (p95/p99)

Team — Alex just pinged about a major p95/p99 regression for Cartograph after what sounds like the catalog update. Looping infra and CS.

What I have so far:
- Customer picked up the stable model alias at ~08:45 PT this morning per their release notes.
- Alerts triggered at 08:55 for elevated 95/99 on embeddings.* routes.
- Cartograph is a high-value expansion account (DEAL-4832) — this needs exec visibility if SLA breaches continue.

Immediate asks: can infra produce a short capsule with the last deployed catalog change, active model variant, and any kernel/quantization changes in the rollout? Prioritize trace correlation for the trace IDs Alex attached.

I will keep Alex updated with cadence. If SRE recommends rollback, we should prepare for a controlled rollback and a PST window.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0192
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Garner <alex.garner@cartograph.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: sudden latency spikes on embeddings endpoint (p95/p99)

Vanessa / team — investigating. Initial findings:
- At 08:40 PT a model-catalog rollout promoted a new embeddings variant (emb-v2-quant) to the "stable" alias for several regions as part of last night's batch candidate promotion.
- emb-v2-quant uses a newly added kernel path intended to reduce cost at long sequence lengths; early microbenchmarks looked fine, but production tail latency increased on padded inputs.
- We see elevated system-level GPU scheduling wait and a larger number of fallback CPU paths for small batches in the affected host pools.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Roll the alias back to emb-v1-stable (fastest to execute, expected to restore previous tail latencies).
2) Apply a routing policy that pins Cartograph traffic to a legacy pool (slower rollout, preserves change for others).

I'll gather traces and a short p95/p99 diff and push an incident dashboard. If we decide rollback, I need a go from Product/Sales for impact communications.

Attaching: traces_cartograph_20260310.txt (short traces), p99_latency_snapshot_20260310.csv

-Markus
Markus Klein
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Garner <alex.garner@cartograph.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 10:35:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: sudden latency spikes on embeddings endpoint (p95/p99)

Alex — thank you for the quick flag and the traces. Our SRE (Markus) verified a correlation with a model-catalog promotion that included emb-v2-quant.

Planned next steps (we will move quickly):
- Short term: We will rollback the stable alias for your region to emb-v1-stable within the next 20 minutes. This is expected to reverse the p95/p99 regressions for your traffic.
- During rollback we'll throttle traffic to reduce risk of cascade; we will monitor your job queue and keep you notified every 15 minutes.
- Post-mortem: We'll run a canary validation on the emb-v2-quant flow with instrumented traces and a synthetic workload that matches your payload shapes before re-promoting.

I appreciate patience — I'll update as soon as the rollback completes.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Alex Garner <alex.garner@cartograph.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 10:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Incident update: rollback complete for Cartograph (embeddings)

On Tue, 10 Mar 2026 10:48:00 -0700 Markus Klein wrote:

Action taken: rolled stable alias back to emb-v1-stable for the us-west region at 10:45 PT.
Observations:
- Post-rollback p95 returned to ~170ms and p99 to ~320ms for Cartograph traffic within two propagation cycles.
- No increased error rate observed after rollback. Throughput returned to expected baselines.

Next steps:
- Run controlled canary of emb-v2-quant in a single pool with synthetic workloads matching Cartograph's request sizes (Marissa owning).
- Add an automatic canary test that validates p95/p99 against a baseline before allowing catalog alias promotion.
- Product will review release checklist to include padding/sequence distribution checks and kernel path perf on small-batch padded inputs.

Markus
Markus Klein
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

On Tue, 10 Mar 2026 11:12:00 -07:00 Vanessa Ortiz wrote to execs: "I will escalate if SLA window is impacted" — per thread context.

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec update requested — Cartograph latency incident closed

Team — documenting final note for execs and the account:
- Timeline: 08:40 promotion -> 08:55 alerts -> 10:45 rollback -> 10:48 normal baseline observed. Impact window ~2 hours.
- Customer impact: degraded search & a small number of timed-out batch jobs; no data loss. Cartograph observed SLA slippage in the window — they requested credit consideration.
- Root cause (preliminary): emb-v2-quant kernel path unexpectedly increases tail latency on padded/small-batch shapes. Failure to validate tail latency on representative payloads before promotion.
- Mitigation taken: rollback, canary plan, canary gating for catalog promotions, and follow-up perf tests.
- Customer comms: Vanessa to send a wrap-up note and offer one-time service credit; Laura to coordinate executive note if Cartograph escalates.

I'll prepare a short incident memo for the leadership thread with attached timelines and charts. Assigning owners: Marissa to run canary validation and report by EOD tomorrow; Markus to add canary gating to the pipeline; Rishi to prepare a scoped credit proposal if Cartograph requests it.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
